01

In Crisis Right Now? Start Here

If you or your family are in immediate danger, or facing housing loss, please use these resources first.

Veterans/Military Crisis Line

24/7 confidential support for veterans and their families in crisis, including safety planning and referrals. Text, call, or chat.

Call or text 988, then press 1
veteranscrisisline.net

211 (National Helpline)

Connects callers to local emergency shelter, food, utility, and rent assistance programs nationwide.

Dial 211
211.org

National Domestic Violence Hotline

Confidential support for anyone experiencing domestic violence, available 24/7.

1-800-799-7233
or text START to 88788

Family Advocacy Program (FAP)

The military's own system for reporting and getting support around domestic abuse or child abuse — distinct from the civilian hotline above, and connected directly to installation resources, safety planning, and command-level intervention when needed.

Contact your installation's Family Advocacy Program office, or ask your installation's Military & Family Support Center to connect you
Available whether or not you want command involved — ask about restricted vs. unrestricted reporting

DoD Safe Helpline

Confidential crisis support and resources specifically for the military community — service members, spouses, and dependents — affected by sexual assault.

1-877-995-5247
or text 55-247 · safehelpline.org, staffed 24/7

National Call Center for Homeless Veterans

24/7 confidential support connecting homeless or at-risk veterans and their families with VA homeless programs, health care, and local resources.

1-877-424-3838
1-877-4AID-VET

Vets4Warriors Peer Support

24/7 confidential peer support staffed entirely by veterans and military family members. Calls answered live, usually in under 30 seconds.

1-855-838-8255
vets4warriors.com · live chat available

Coaching Into Care

A free VA phone service for family members and friends worried about a veteran, offering guidance on starting the conversation and encouraging treatment.

1-888-823-7458
Mon–Fri, 8am–8pm ET

Chaplain Support — Active Duty

Every installation has a chaplain on call, and conversations with a chaplain are 100% confidential — protected communication that can't be reported to command, unlike most other support channels. No appointment needed for a crisis.

Contact your unit chaplain, installation chapel, or the Command Duty Officer (CDO) after hours
Military OneSource can also help you locate one · 1-800-342-9647

Chaplain Support — Veterans

VA Chaplain Service (Spiritual Care) is available at every VA medical center, offering confidential support regardless of religious affiliation or belief — open to veterans of any faith or none at all.

Ask for Chaplain Service / Spiritual Care at your local VA medical center
va.gov/find-locations to locate the nearest facility
Take Action Save the Veterans Crisis Line (988, press 1) and Vets4Warriors (1-855-838-8255) to your phone before you need them. In a crisis, looking up a number costs precious time.
Did you know Chaplains are one of the only resources with fully privileged communication — for active duty, a chaplain cannot report what's shared with command, even in ways a mental health provider sometimes must. That confidentiality is often exactly what makes it easier to talk.

Chaplain & Spiritual Care Support, by Branch

Chaplain support isn't a single national hotline — it's reached locally, through your specific branch, installation, or VA facility. Here's who to contact depending on your situation.

Army

Contact your unit chaplain or the Installation Religious Support Office (chapel). Available 24/7 through the Staff Duty Officer after hours. Fully confidential — not reportable to command.

Navy & Marine Corps

Contact your command chaplain or the installation chapel. The Chaplain Corps also provides chaplains aboard ships and to deployed Marine units — ask your Command Duty Officer to reach the duty chaplain after hours.

Air Force & Space Force

Contact your Wing Chaplain's office or installation chapel. After hours, Command Post or the Wing Command Post can connect you to the on-call chaplain.

Coast Guard

Coast Guard chaplain support is provided through a partnership with the Navy Chaplain Corps. Contact your unit or nearest Coast Guard chapel, or ask your command for the supporting Navy chaplain.

National Guard & Reserve

Contact your unit chaplain or your state's Joint Force Headquarters State Chaplain's Office — especially useful since Guard/Reserve families often don't live near an installation. Yellow Ribbon Reintegration Program events also include chaplain support.

Veterans (any era, any discharge status)

VA Chaplain Service (Spiritual Care) is available at every VA medical center — ask for Chaplain Service at check-in or by phone. Open to veterans of any faith, or none. Some Vet Centers can also refer you to VA chaplain support.

Can't reach your local chaplain directly?

Military OneSource can help locate the right chaplain resource for your branch and situation: 1-800-342-9647, available 24/7. For veterans, your local VA medical center's main line can always connect you to Chaplain Service — find yours at va.gov/find-locations.

Worth confirming locallyExact contact procedures (which office, which phone tree) vary by installation and can change. This page reflects the general structure used across the services — always confirm the current process with your specific installation, unit, or VA facility.

For Spouses of Veterans with PTSD

Loving someone with PTSD carries its own weight — these resources are built specifically for the spouse or partner, not just the veteran.

NAMI Homefront

A free 6-session education program from the National Alliance on Mental Illness, built specifically for family members and caregivers of service members and veterans — covering PTSD, TBI, depression, and how to care for yourself while supporting them.

1-800-950-6264
or text "HelpLine" to 62640 · nami.org/Homefront

VA Caregiver Support Line

A direct line for spouses and family caregivers of veterans, including those managing the effects of PTSD — connects you to a licensed Caregiver Support Coordinator, support groups, and respite care options.

1-855-260-3274
caregiver.va.gov

PTSD Foundation of America

Peer mentoring for combat veterans alongside dedicated support groups for spouses and family members affected by a loved one's combat PTSD, through their Camp Hope program.

1-877-717-8262
ptsdusa.org

Military & Family Life Counseling (MFLC)

Free, confidential, non-medical counseling for military spouses available through installation Family Support Centers — no paperwork, no records kept, and no referral needed to talk through the strain of supporting a partner with PTSD.

1-800-342-9647
Ask your installation's Military & Family Support Center, or via Military OneSource

Operation Purple Healing Adventures

A free retreat-style program from the National Military Family Association, built specifically for military families who've experienced combat stress, PTSD, or TBI — spouses and children included, not just the veteran.

militaryfamily.org

The Independence Fund — Caregiver Fellowship

Direct grants and support specifically for the spouse or family caregiver of a catastrophically injured or ill veteran — recognizing the caregiver's own toll, not just the veteran's recovery.

independencefund.org
Did you knowYou don't need your veteran's participation to get support for yourself. NAMI Homefront, MFLC, and the VA Caregiver Support Line are all designed for you to reach out on your own behalf.

Understanding & Treating PTSD

PTSD is one of the most common invisible wounds among veterans, and it affects spouses and families too. PTSD Family Coach and Coaching Into Care are both built for family members — not just veterans — and you don't need a formal diagnosis in the house to use either one. Vet Center counseling, Give an Hour, and Military OneSource counseling are all available before things reach a breaking point.

Did you know You don't need a diagnosis to ask for help. These resources exist for support and prevention, not only crisis response.
Common mistake Waiting for a crisis before reaching out. Support is available well before things reach a breaking point.

A Closer Look: Chapter 35 Education Benefits

Chapter 35 (formerly the Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance program, or DEA) is one of the most valuable and most under-claimed benefits available to military spouses and children.

Who qualifies

The spouse or child of a veteran rated 100% permanently and totally disabled from a service-connected condition, or who died while on active duty or from a service-connected condition.

What it pays (2025–2026 rate)

Up to $1,574/month for full-time enrollment, paid directly to you — not the school. Lower for part-time; adjusts each October.

How long it lasts

Up to 36 months of benefits (45 months if you began using DEA before August 1, 2018) — for a degree, certificate, apprenticeship, or on-the-job training.

Time limits

Children generally eligible ages 18–26. Spouses generally have a 10-year window from the date VA determines eligibility — confirm your specific window with VA.

How to apply

Apply online at va.gov or submit VA Form 22-5490 to the VA regional processing office for your state. va.gov/education/survivor-dependent-benefits/dependents-education-assistance

Did you know — Fry Scholarship vs. Chapter 35The Fry Scholarship usually pays more than Chapter 35 (100% of tuition, plus housing and books), but you can only use one at a time. If the veteran died in the line of duty after 9/10/2001, compare both before you enroll.

A Closer Look: SSDI Fast-Track for 100% Disabled Veterans

Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) is separate from VA disability compensation — you can receive both — but veterans with the highest VA ratings can skip to the front of the line.

Who qualifies for expedited processing

Veterans with a VA disability rating of 100% Permanent & Total. Separately, anyone (any VA rating) disabled while on active duty on/after October 1, 2001 qualifies under SSA's "Wounded Warrior" provision — doesn't need to be combat-related.

What "expedited" means

SSA flags the claim as a Military Casualty/Wounded Warrior case, cutting the wait from months (sometimes years) down to weeks. It does not guarantee approval — SSDI uses its own separate disability standard.

How to make sure it's flagged

Don't count on automatic data-sharing. When you apply (online, by phone at 1-800-772-1213, or in person) write "Veteran 100% P&T" in the Remarks section, or clearly state Wounded Warrior status, and attach a copy of the VA notification letter.

Common mistakeAssuming a 100% VA rating guarantees SSDI. It doesn't — a 100% P&T rating only speeds up the review; SSA can still deny the claim under its own standard.
Pro tipSelf-identify — don't assume SSA already knows. Say the magic words — "Veteran 100% P&T" or "Wounded Warrior" — and attach the VA letter yourself. ssa.gov/people/veterans

A Closer Look: Student Loan Discharge for 100% Disabled Veterans

Veterans rated 100% Permanent & Total by the VA can have their federal student loans fully discharged — meaning the remaining balance no longer has to be repaid. This is a separate benefit from SSDI and from VA disability compensation itself.

Who qualifies

Veterans with a VA disability rating of 100% Permanent & Total (P&T) qualify for Total and Permanent Disability (TPD) Discharge of federal student loans — Direct Loans, FFEL Program loans, and Federal Perkins Loans.

How it happens

The Department of Education periodically matches records with the VA and Social Security Administration and can identify and notify eligible borrowers automatically. Don't rely on this alone — you can also apply directly.

How to apply if it isn't automatic

Submit your VA disability documentation through the TPD Discharge application, either online or by mailing it to the discharge servicer along with proof of your 100% P&T rating.

disabilitydischarge.com

Did you knowDischarged student loan debt due to disability has, in recent years, been treated as not taxable at the federal level — a change from older rules where forgiven debt counted as income. Tax treatment can shift with legislation, so confirm current federal and state tax treatment with a tax professional before assuming it's fully tax-free.
Common mistakeAssuming this discharge is automatic and doing nothing. If you haven't received a notice despite qualifying, apply directly rather than waiting — the data match doesn't always catch every eligible veteran.

A Closer Look: Veteran & Military Spouse Tax Benefits

Tax rules touch almost every benefit in this guide — here's how the major pieces fit together. Federal rules are fairly consistent; state rules vary widely, so treat the state-level items as a starting point for your own research, not a final answer.

VA disability compensation

Not taxable at the federal or state level. This applies whether it's paid alone or alongside other benefits.

CRSC (Combat-Related Special Compensation)

Tax-free, for retirees with combat-related disabilities who qualify for concurrent receipt of both retirement pay and VA compensation.

CRDP (Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay)

Unlike CRSC, CRDP is simply restored military retirement pay — and military retirement pay is generally taxable at the federal level, even when received alongside tax-free VA compensation.

State property tax exemptions

Most states offer at least a partial property tax exemption for disabled veterans, and many offer a full exemption for veterans rated 100% P&T. The exact threshold, amount, and application process is entirely state-specific.

State income tax on military retirement pay

A majority of states now fully exempt military retirement pay from state income tax, though a handful still tax some or all of it. Confirm your specific state's current rule directly.

MSRRA (Military Spouse Residency Relief Act)

Lets a military spouse keep their tax residency and voter registration in their home state, even after a PCS move to a new state — preventing a spouse from being forced to pay income tax in every state they're stationed in.

Free tax filing help

MilTax (through Military OneSource) offers free tax prep and e-filing software built for military-specific tax situations, available to active duty, Guard/Reserve, and some recently separated veterans and their families. militaryonesource.mil/miltax

VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) sites, often located on-installation, offer free in-person tax preparation from IRS-certified volunteers.

Worth confirmingTax law — especially at the state level — changes often and varies by where you're stationed or living. Treat every figure and rule above as a starting point, and confirm current details with a tax professional or your state's department of revenue before filing.

Housing, Relocation & PCS

From homeless prevention to home loans to the logistics of a permanent-change-of-station move.

HUD-VASH Program

HUD/VA Supportive Housing combines rental assistance with case management for homeless veterans and their families.

va.gov/homeless/hud-vash.asp

SSVF — Supportive Services for Veteran Families

VA-funded, community-based rental assistance and case management to prevent homelessness or rapidly rehouse veteran families — can cover deposits, past-due rent, and utilities. Recent program changes have extended temporary rental assistance up to 10 months for eligible households, though the exact duration and amount depend on your local SSVF grantee and case circumstances.

va.gov/homeless/ssvf · find your local SSVF provider through the VA homeless programs office

VA Home Loan Program

Spouses may be eligible as a co-borrower, and unremarried surviving spouses of veterans who died in service or from a service-connected condition may qualify independently for a Certificate of Eligibility.

va.gov/family-and-caregiver-benefits/housing-assistance

VA Specially Adapted Housing (SAH) & Special Housing Adaptation (SHA) Grants

VA grants — not loans — to help veterans with certain service-connected disabilities (loss of limb use, blindness, severe burns, and similar) build, buy, or modify a home for accessibility.

va.gov/housing-assistance/disability-housing-grants

Homes For Our Troops

Builds and gifts specially adapted, mortgage-free custom homes for severely injured post-9/11 veterans — no cost to the veteran or their family.

hfotusa.org

Building Homes for Heroes

Provides mortgage-free homes or home modifications for wounded, ill, or injured veterans and their families.

buildinghomesforheroes.org

Veterans Community Project

Tiny-home villages offering transitional housing paired with case management and wraparound support for homeless veterans, with locations in several cities.

veteranscommunityproject.org

Military Housing Office / PCS Support

On-installation relocation assistance, including move planning, temporary lodging, and housing referral services.

Contact your installation's Military & Family Support Center

Salute To Home Housing Assistance & Case Management

One-on-one case management to help veteran families find stable housing and connect to the full range of available benefits.

www.salutetohome.com
Worth confirmingThe 10-month rental assistance figure for SSVF reflects a recent program change we couldn't independently verify against a live source. Confirm the current cap, amount, and eligibility directly with your local SSVF grantee or VA homeless programs office before relying on it for planning.

Legal Assistance

Federal protections, free legal help, and — if your veteran has an error or injustice on their military record — the correction boards that can fix it, sometimes years after the fact.

Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA)

Federal legal protections covering leases, evictions, interest rate caps, and other financial matters for service members and, in some cases, dependents during active duty.

Ask your installation Legal Assistance Office about SCRA protections

American Bar Association Military Pro Bono Project

Connects active-duty service members (typically via a JAG legal assistance office) with volunteer civilian attorneys for family law, housing, and consumer issues.

militaryprobono.org

Installation Legal Assistance Office

Free legal consultations for active-duty families on wills, powers of attorney, and family law questions.

Contact your local installation Legal Assistance Office

Stateside Legal

Free self-help legal information website built specifically for military families.

statesidelegal.org

Lawyers Serving Warriors

Free estate planning legal documents — wills, powers of attorney, and advance medical directives — prepared by volunteer attorneys for combat-wounded veterans and their families.

lawyersservingwarriors.com

Veterans Treatment Court

A specialized court docket, now operating in many counties, that diverts veterans facing criminal charges — often tied to PTSD, TBI, or substance use — into a treatment-focused track instead of standard prosecution. Veterans are paired with a fellow veteran mentor and connected to VA services as part of the process, rather than facing incarceration alone.

Ask the defense attorney or public defender whether your county has a Veterans Treatment Court, or search "[your county] Veterans Treatment Court"

National Veterans Legal Services Program (NVLSP)

Free legal help specifically for appealing denied or underrated VA disability claims — distinct from a VSO, and often brought in for more complex or repeatedly denied cases.

nvlsp.org

Military Records Correction Boards

If your veteran has an error or injustice on their military record — a bad discharge characterization, an incorrect disability rating, a wrongly-worded evaluation — these boards can fix it.

BoardCoversSite
Board for Correction of Naval Records (BCNR)Navy & Marine Corps — active, reserve, retired, formersecnav.navy.mil/mra/bcnr
Army Board for Correction of Military Records (ABCMR)Army, Army Reserve, Army National Guardarba.army.pentagon.mil
Coast Guard BCMRCurrent & former Coast Guard, incl. Reserve (under DHS, not DoD)uscg.mil/Resources/legal/BCMR
Air Force/Space Force BCMR (AFBCMR)Regular, Guard, and Reserve Airmen and Guardiansafrba-portal.cce.af.mil

How to apply

File DD Form 149 (Application for Correction of Military Record) with supporting documents — orders, medical records, VA decisions, evaluations, sworn statements. Lower-level administrative options must be exhausted first. No fee to file.

Filing deadline

Technically within 3 years of discovering the error, but boards routinely waive this "in the interest of justice," especially for PTSD, TBI, or MST cases.

How long it takes

By law, 90% of cases decided within 10 months, all within 18 months — contested cases can run longer.

Did you knowBCNR is a "court of last review." For Navy and Marine Corps discharges, its decisions are final agency actions — challengeable only in federal court from there.
Common mistakeFiling with the wrong board. If it's been under 15 years since discharge and you only want a discharge upgrade, file with the Discharge Review Board (DD Form 293) first — it's faster. Save the Correction Board (DD Form 149) for cases past 15 years or needing broader relief (pay, ratings, promotions).

How to Actually Get Child Care Fee Assistance

The process runs through two connected systems, and knowing how they work together saves a lot of frustration:

Step 1 — MilitaryChildCare.com profile

Required starting point for on-base waitlists, off-base fee assistance, and respite care requests. All programs run through this single household profile.

Step 2 — Apply through Child Care Aware of America

CCAoA administers fee assistance on behalf of your branch. Identify a licensed provider, then submit paperwork (incl. the provider's tax ID) through the Fee Assistance Enrollment Portal. 1-800-424-2246 (8am–7pm ET, Mon–Fri)

PCS child care travel reimbursement

If you've requested full-time care at your installation's child development center, been waitlisted, and told care won't be available within 30 days of arrival, you may be reimbursed up to $1,500 for travel expenses to bring a designated caregiver to your new duty station. Ask your gaining installation's CYS office.

Respite care for special circumstances

Families with a deployed service member, or enrolled in EFMP, may qualify for additional no-cost, hourly respite child care — ask your installation's Child and Youth Services office.

Pro TipOne profile unlocks everything. Create your MilitaryChildCare.com household profile before you even have a specific need — waitlists, fee assistance, and respite care all pull from that same profile.
09

Free Retreats & Camps for Veteran Families

Many reputable nonprofits fund fully-paid retreats, camps, and getaways for veteran and military families — covering lodging, meals, and often travel. These are legitimate 501(c)(3) organizations with established track records, though space is limited and most require an application.

Family & Couples Retreats

Project Sanctuary

Free six-day therapeutic retreats for military and veteran families (and separate couples retreats), plus two years of follow-up family support. About 20 retreats a year across several states.

1-855-838-8255
projectsanctuary.us

Boulder Crest — Family R&R Stays

Free 2–7 night stays for veteran families to rest and reconnect, separate from clinical PATHH programs. Also offers Couples PATHH, a free 5-day program for partners.

bouldercrest.org

Boulder Crest — Warrior PATHH

A free 7-day immersive retreat (part of an 18-month program) for combat veterans built around post-traumatic growth, with separate tracks for male and female veterans.

bouldercrest.org

Operation Red Wings Foundation

Free retreats for veterans, spouses, couples, and families, run in sequence — individual, then couples, then family retreat for veterans; spouses may attend in any order.

orwfoundation.org

Semper Fi & America's Fund — Odyssey Retreat

A six-day transition retreat for wounded, critically ill, or injured service members and their families covering life-planning, employment, and reintegration support.

thefund.org

Warfighter Advance

Free peer-to-peer intensive retreats for veterans with PTSD or TBI — and, notably, separate retreats built specifically for spouses navigating a partner's combat-related PTSD, not just joint family programming.

warfighteradvance.org

Vail Veterans Program

Free outdoor recreation retreats in Vail, Colorado — skiing, adaptive sports, and summer programming — for wounded, ill, or injured service members and their families.

vailveteransprogram.org

Higher Ground Sun Valley

Adaptive sports and outdoor therapeutic retreats in Idaho for veterans with PTSD, TBI, or physical injuries, with family programming included.

highergroundusa.org

Kids, Youth & Grief-Focused Programs

Operation Purple Camp

National Military Family Association's free week-long sleepaway camp for military-connected kids.

militaryfamily.org

Camp Corral

Free week-long summer camp (ages 8–15) for children of wounded, ill, injured, or fallen military service members, funded largely by Golden Corral. A small "hold my spot" deposit applies.

campcorral.org

Snowball Express

Gary Sinise Foundation's free week-long sleepaway camp for military-connected kids ages 6–17, at locations nationwide. Families cover only transportation and a refundable deposit.

snowballexpress.org

TAPS Good Grief Camps

Free camps for children and teens grieving a service member's death, paired with military mentors, plus a National Military Survivor Seminar over Memorial Day weekend and a 24/7 survivor helpline.

1-800-959-8277
taps.org
Common mistakeAssuming a free retreat must be a scam. Before applying anywhere, confirm 501(c)(3) status and check ratings on Charity Navigator or GuideStar/Candid — it takes five minutes.
Pro TipA small refundable deposit (common for kids' camps) is normal, not a red flag. What is a red flag: any request for full banking information, a wire transfer, or a non-refundable payment.
10

Discounts & Free Tickets for Veterans

Free or deeply discounted access to sports, entertainment, museums, and public lands. Eligibility (active duty vs. veteran vs. retiree) changes fairly often — always double-check current terms before you plan around one.

Tickets, Parks & Museums

Vet Tix

Free tickets donated by sports teams, venues, and promoters — sporting events, concerts, theater, family shows. Open to currently serving military, honorably discharged veterans of all eras, and immediate family of those killed in action.

vettix.org

America the Beautiful — Interagency Military Pass

Free lifetime pass for veterans and Gold Star Families (free annual pass for active-duty + dependents) covering entrance fees at 2,000+ federal recreation sites.

store.usgs.gov/MilitaryPass · nps.gov

Blue Star Museums

Free admission each summer (Armed Forces Day–Labor Day) to 2,000+ museums, zoos, and cultural sites for active-duty military and families. Active-duty only — not veterans/retirees generally.

arts.gov/BlueStarMuseums

Waves of Honor

SeaWorld, Busch Gardens, Sesame Place — active-duty members plus up to 3 dependents get one complimentary admission per year.

waves-of-honor.com

Movies & Entertainment

AMC Theatres

Military discount available, redeemable only in person at the box office (not online) at participating locations.

amctheatres.com/discounts

Regal Cinemas

Discounted tickets for active-duty and retired military at participating locations; discount level varies by theater.

regmovies.com/military-discount

Cinemark

Discounted tickets for active and retired military members at participating locations — bring your ID to the box office.

cinemark.com/discounts/military-discount

Retail, Travel & Verification

The Home Depot

10% off in-store and online, extended to all U.S. veterans, active-duty, and military spouses. Pre-register via app or website to use it online.

homedepot.com

Lowe's

10% off for military, veterans, and their spouses, both in-store and online.

lowes.com/l/military-discount

Airline Military Fares

Most major U.S. carriers offer unpublished military leisure fares, extra checked bags, and early boarding — generally not bookable online. Call the airline's military reservations line directly.

Rental Cars

Avis/Budget/Hertz/Thrifty/Dollar: ~5–25% off, occasional upgrades. Enterprise/National/Alamo: ~5% off, no membership required. WeSalute+ (Hertz): up to 35% off with a membership code.

hertz.com · enterprise.com · wesalute.com

ID.me & GovX

The identity-verification services behind most "verify your military status" discount buttons. Create a free account once, verify with proof of service or a .mil email, and reuse it across participating brands.

id.me · govx.com

Financial & Everyday Services

USAA

Banking, insurance, and financial products available to veterans, active-duty service members, and their eligible family members — often cited for member-focused service and competitive rates, though it's worth comparing against other options for your specific needs.

usaa.com

Wireless Carrier Discounts

Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile all offer ongoing military/veteran discounts on select plans — typically 15–25% off, verified through ID.me or a similar service at signup.

Texas Roadhouse

Many locations offer an everyday military discount (not just Veterans Day), though it varies by franchise — worth asking at your local restaurant.

Great Clips & Sport Clips

Great Clips offers an ongoing military discount at many locations. Sport Clips runs "Haircuts for Our Heroes," providing free haircuts to troops before deployment through participating stores and USO partnerships.

Big Trips

Shades of Green (Walt Disney World)

An Armed Forces Recreation Center resort located inside Walt Disney World, offering below-market rates exclusively to active-duty, Guard/Reserve, veterans with a VA disability rating, and retirees.

shadesofgreen.org

Armed Forces Vacation Club

Discounted resort condo stays worldwide, plus special military ticket pricing for Disney, Universal, and other major attractions — available to a broad range of military-affiliated and veteran status categories.

afvclub.com

Six Flags Military Discount

Discounted admission for active-duty, veterans, and their families at participating Six Flags parks — offer details vary by park and season.

sixflags.com/military

Space-A (Space Available) Travel

Free standby seats on military aircraft, offered after all official passengers and cargo are accounted for. Open to active duty on leave and military retirees (unlimited, worldwide), and — worth knowing — to veterans rated 100% Permanent & Total and Medal of Honor recipients, plus eligible dependents in some categories. There's no advance ticket: you sign up at the passenger terminal and get called by priority category, and flights can be delayed or canceled without notice, so it takes real flexibility.

Check schedules through your local passenger terminal or Air Mobility Command's Space-A page
Did you knowBlue Star Museums is active-duty only — unlike most programs on this page, it does not cover veterans or retirees generally. Some individual museums extend discounts further, so it's worth asking.
Worth confirmingSpace-A eligibility runs on a tiered priority system (Category I through VI) that depends on your specific status — active duty, retiree, disabled veteran, or dependent — and whether you're traveling accompanied or unaccompanied. The general shape above is accurate, but confirm your exact category and current rules with your local passenger terminal before planning a trip around it.
Take ActionSet up your ID.me or GovX profile today, even before you have a specific purchase in mind. Once verified, you can reuse it instantly at hundreds of participating retailers.

Salute To Home Foundation exists to make sure no veteran or veteran family faces housing instability alone. Our services include:

Emergency Shelter

Emergency shelter for veterans and their families.

Meals & Basic Needs

Meals and basic-needs support.

Housing Assistance

Housing assistance and rapid rehousing referrals.

Case Management
